claim: A user can explicitly publish a deterministic, independently verified project/participant registration signed by the installation key into bounded shared project state; it converges and reopens offline, while remaining self-registration evidence rather than identity, enrollment, a role, shared revocation, or relay authority.
commands: node ../scripts/run-with-heartbeat.mjs --timeout-seconds 120 --heartbeat-seconds 30 -- npm exec vitest run src/workspace/deviceIdentity.test.ts src/workspace/projectDeviceDirectory.test.ts src/workspace/ResearchPresence.ui.test.tsx src/workspace/researchStateInspection.test.ts src/workspace/signedPresencePublisher.test.ts src/workspace/presenceModel.test.ts
proved: The same generated Ed25519 installation key signs independently domain-separated ephemeral presence and deterministic project registration claims; Rust output verifies in Node WebCrypto and six signed-field mutations fail.
Strict frontend parsing requires exact fields, canonical base64url, exact key/signature sizes, stable project/participant IDs, recomputed key IDs, and the expected project.
Explicit registration stores one exact key/project/participant-bound Yjs settings record; idempotent writes, disconnected distinct-device merge, and offline full-state reopen pass.
Reads cap registration records and total settings scans, verify in batches of eight, block writes on poison/bounds, retain same-key participant conflicts, and never select an identity.

Drive/live product UI requires explicit publication and discloses stable-key correlation, persistence, self-reported names, and no identity/role/access effect; durable offline entries can receive local-only approval labels.
The existing read-only MCP research inspection returns bounded public fingerprints, participant IDs, conflict/integrity counts, and no invalid record body or mutation route.
notProved: A registration is trusted enrollment, an authenticated person or organization, a project role, shared approval/revocation, or relay authorization.
A bearer peer cannot replay deterministic registrations, publish arbitrary self-issued keys, delete registrations, or flood shared Yjs state within broader transport limits.
The stable public key avoids cross-project correlation; correlation is an explicit consequence disclosed before publication.
Local approval state propagates to collaborators, disconnects a peer, revokes an invitation, or blocks Yjs/MCP operations.
Durable policy/scenario/review events are signed, key rotation/recovery exists, or physical packaged two-install/five-client gates have passed.
